U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Industrial Technologies (2002). Energy and Environmental Profile of the U.S. Mining Industry, Chapter 7: Gold & Silver. Prepared by BCS, Incorporated, September 2002. Washington, DC: U.S. DOE. Chapter 7 only (20 pages, printed 7-1 to 7-20); no report number or DOI printed on the chapter.

Locators are printed chapter pages (7-n; PDF page = n). The only technology-level numbers are Tables 7-2 (surface gold mine fleet) and 7-3 (beneficiation/processing), MODEL estimates by BCS (SHERPA) for one hypothetical 15,000 short-ton/day US mine, in Btu per short ton of ore (All units column), converted to GJ/t or kWh/t. Carrier from the table footnotes: Table 7-2 footnote a = diesel (trucks, dozers, loaders, shovel, lighting, tanker, bulk truck, grader) and b = electricity (rotary drills, pumps); Table 7-3 footnote a = electricity (SAG, ball, electrowinning) and b = diesel (washing). Smelting and refining have no footnote marker, so target total. The request asked for energy by step for heap leach, CIL/CIP, carbon regeneration kiln, electrowinning and smelting: this chapter gives energy ONLY for SAG and ball mills, smelting, refining, washing and electrowinning; there is NO energy figure for heap leach, CIL/CIP, the carbon kiln (temperature and cycle time only) or the leach tanks; and heap-leach opex is only an upper bound (less than USD 2 per ton ore). Traps: (1) Per-ton figures of the haul truck row include waste hauling (9.7 t waste per t ore), so are per t ore, not per t material. (2) Footnote letters are not consistent between tables (a = diesel in Table 7-2 but electricity in Table 7-3). (3) Table 7-1 industry statistics and 1976 BoM whole-chain values are in other-values. (4) Printed short tons. No capex, no TRL.
